summary.headline: Sagar Cements Q2 FY27 volumes rose 26% YoY, but loss after tax of ₹52 crore; management guides FY27 EBITDA of ₹350-375 crore.
summary.overview: Volumes grew 26% YoY and revenue 17% YoY in Q2 FY27, but elevated fuel, packaging and freight costs and planned maintenance shutdowns (Mattampally, Jeerabad) weighed on profitability, with EBITDA of ₹265 per ton and a loss after tax of ₹52 crore. Management said the company has hit its margin bottom and expects H2 recovery driven by South price hikes of about ₹25 per bag on average (roughly ₹500 per ton realisation uplift). FY27 EBITDA guidance was revised to ₹350-375 crore (about ₹525 per ton) from the earlier ~₹410 crore projection. Net debt has peaked with CapEx largely complete and is expected to decline from Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Plant utilisation (Q2)
segments.commentary: Mattampally 73%, Gudipadu 85%, Bayyavaram 52%, Jeerabad 72%, Jajpur 38%, Dachepalli 57%. Andhra plant (3 MTPA) earned ₹402 per ton per analyst question and is still 20,000-30,000 tons per month short of breakeven volume.

segments.name: Superfine Building Materials (new)
segments.commentary: Board approved CapEx; microsilica operations at Galsi, West Bengal to start by end of Q3. Ultrafine GGBS at Bayyavaram expected to show results from mid-Q4; EBITDA of ₹25-30 crore assumed for FY28 at 35-40% margins, with CapEx of ₹60-80 crore over 18 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cement volume guidance of approximately 7 million tonnes, cement only (excludes clinker).
FY27 EBITDA revised to ₹350-375 crore (roughly ₹525 per ton), versus earlier projection of about ₹410 crore.
H2 FY27 EBITDA assumed around ₹650 per ton, driven by ~₹500 realisation uplift and ~₹200 fuel cost increase; ₹50-75 per ton savings held as contingency.
Q3 FY27 margin environment of around ₹650 per ton if prices hold.
FY28 volume target of 8-8.25 million tons with capacity utilisation of 65-70%; pencilled EBITDA around ₹650 per ton, roughly ₹500 crore.

Net debt to stabilise in Q3 FY27 and decline from Q4 FY27; around ₹250 crore debt reduction from FY28 plus Vizag land monetisation; stated goal to halve net debt from ~₹1,450-1,600 crore over two years.
Vizag land monetisation of ₹350 crore net value, with around ₹150 crore advance expected in FY27.
Jeerabad incentive at ₹30 crore per year, with a further ₹50 crore expected over the remaining two and a half years.
capex_capacity: Capacity now 11.75 million tons after commissioning 0.75 MTPA grinding unit in Andhra during Q2.
Commissioned 4.35 MW waste heat recovery at Gudipadu and a 0.5 MTPA expansion at Jeerabad recently.
Remaining WHRS at Andhra scheduled for FY28, expected to save ₹1.5 crore per month; 7-8 MW solar at Jeerabad expected to save ₹4-4.5 crore per year.
Most CapEx complete; minor cash flow may spill into Q1 FY28. Q3 CapEx to be roughly flat with Q2 levels.
Superfine division: Galsi (West Bengal) microsilica and Bayyavaram ultrafine GGBS, with ₹60-80 crore CapEx and ₹20 crore working capital projected.
demand_pricing: South prices: ₹20 per bag hike in non-trade and ₹20 in trade from August to September; a further ₹20 in non-trade and ₹5 in trade from September to October.
Other regions: ₹5-10 per bag in Madhya Pradesh, ₹5 in Odisha, Maharashtra largely flat after adjustment, others flat.
Average realisation uplift at Sagar of about ₹25 per bag (roughly ₹500 per ton) from end-August through October; GST correction to be netted off.
YTD demand growth: AP and Telangana about 15%, Tamil Nadu about 10%, Kerala about 12%, Maharashtra about 10%, MP 7.5-8%, Gujarat about 5%, Karnataka 2-3%, Odisha flat.
Management says trade and non-trade margins are similar; optical trade realisations are higher due to discounts being invoiced separately.
Cement prices were soft in July and August before partial recovery in September; management sees the South price bottom reached for Sagar but not necessarily for the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why are standalone plants earning less than Andhra, and when do they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Mattampally and Jeerabad were under maintenance shutdowns, with Mattampally a long and expensive one; management expects all units to match or beat Andhra in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: When will Andhra break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational breakeven is expected in H2 FY27 or at least Q1 FY28, as volumes are 20,000-30,000 tons per month short of required levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised full-year EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: ₹350-375 crore for FY27, roughly ₹525 per ton, against an earlier projection of about ₹410 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What fuel cost increase is assumed, and what if the company moves to spot prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel is covered up to end-January at below ₹2 per 1,000 kcal, with a ₹200 per ton increase up to August; management assumes another ₹200 per ton if buying at spot.

qa_highlights.question: Is the net debt going to fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is expected to stay flat in Q3 FY27 and decline sharply from Q4, with around ₹250 crore reduction from FY28 plus Vizag land proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 EBITDA per ton and volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pencils in around ₹650 per ton on 8-8.25 million tons, or roughly ₹500 crore EBITDA for FY28.

risks_watch: Input cost pressure from West Asia geopolitical developments: fuel and freight (diesel) rising; freight at a five-quarter high of ₹900 per ton.
Price hikes realised mainly in late September and October; sustainability of ~₹500 per ton realisation uplift is untested and net of GST correction.
Andhra plant breakeven (₹127 crore annual interest burden) and volume gap of 20,000-30,000 tons per month.
Net debt of ~₹1,450-1,600 crore and ROCE described as extremely low; deleveraging depends on Vizag land sale (₹150 crore advance targeted in FY27).
Fuel covered only to end-January; spot exposure could require another ~₹200 per ton of price hikes.
Management reduced disclosure of plant-wise utilisation and quarterly net debt in the presentation; analysts asked for restoration.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the demand outlook and H2 margin recovery, with specific numerical guidance, but cautious on industry-wide pricing ("I would reserve my comments"). Evasive on exact Q3 margin and on Andhra breakeven timing, which management hedged as "if not in the current year".
key_quotes: So, I would say that we have already hit our bottom when it comes to our own margins.
We remain confident of achieving our FY '27 volume guidance of approximately 7 million tonnes supported by our expanded capacity and improving demand outlook.
Demand, I think, we are going to hit highs every quarter from here on.

growth.why: FY27 volume guided at ~7 MT (held) and FY27 EBITDA cut to ₹350-375 crore from ~₹410 crore; H2 recovery rests on ~₹25/bag (~₹500/t) South price hikes, with FY28 volume target of 8-8.25 MT at 65-70% utilisation and Superfine capex (₹60-80 crore) as new growth, but the brief gives no hard order book behind the price-led recovery.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management assumes H2 FY27 EBITDA of around ₹650 per ton, driven by ~₹500 per ton realisation uplift from South price hikes against ~₹200 per ton fuel cost increase, versus Q2 consolidated EBITDA of ₹265 per ton; the price hikes are untested and partly netted off by GST correction.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Galsi microsilica (₹60 crore capex) is due by end of Q3 and Bayyavaram ultrafine GGBS results from mid-Q4, while the Andhra WHRS is slated for FY28; capacity already rose to 11.75 MTPA with the 0.75 MTPA Andhra grinding unit and the 0.5 MTPA Jeerabad expansion.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 volume guidance of ~7 MT is held after 26% YoY Q2 growth, and FY28 target is 8-8.25 MT (about 14-18% above FY27), but Andhra is still 20,000-30,000 tons per month short of breakeven and several plants ran at 38-57% utilisation.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says most capex is complete and Q3 capex is roughly flat with Q2, with the Superfine ₹60-80 crore already approved, and net debt of ~₹1,450-1,600 crore is the stated priority for deleveraging.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA was just cut to ₹350-375 crore from ~₹410 crore, so an upgrade depends on the ~₹500 per ton South price uplift holding and the ₹50-75 per ton cost savings contingency materialising.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fuel is covered only to end-January, with spot buying adding another ~₹200 per ton, and freight is at a five-quarter high of ₹900 per ton; management also flagged cautious industry-wide pricing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Superfine division launches microsilica at Galsi by end of Q3 and ultrafine GGBS at Bayyavaram from mid-Q4, with FY28 EBITDA of ₹25-30 crore assumed at 35-40% margins.

rows.label: Net debt peaks and declines from Q4 FY27
rows.why: Net debt is to stabilise in Q3 FY27 and fall from Q4, with ~₹250 crore reduction from FY28 plus ₹150 crore Vizag land advance expected in FY27 (₹350 crore total).

rows.label: Andhra plant operational breakeven
rows.why: Andhra (3 MTPA) earned ₹402 per ton and is 20,000-30,000 tons per month short of breakeven volume against ₹127 crore annual interest burden, with management hedging on timing.

rows.label: South price hikes of ~₹25 per bag stick
rows.why: South hikes of ₹40 per bag in trade and non-trade through October (about ₹25 per bag average, ~₹500 per ton) are untested, and management is not sure industry prices have bottomed.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 volume (~7 MT), the FY28 8-8.25 MT target and H2 margin recovery, but cautious on industry-wide pricing and evasive on Q3 margin and Andhra breakeven timing; analysts pushed on the cut to FY27 EBITDA, the fuel spot exposure and restoring plant-wise and quarterly net
